newsitem.title: USA: Israel foreign minister says West Bank violence planned.
newsitem.headline: Israel foreign minister says West Bank violence planned.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Thursday he believed the violence in the West Bank and Gaza was planned in advance and he called on Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to prove he is a partner for peace by bringing it under control.

Speaking to reporters after meeting Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller here, Levy said, "The slightest Middle East wind could have brought about these developments. In my opinion, these steps were planned in advance."

He vowed that Israel would continue the peace process but "would not allow violence to threaten us," adding that Arafat "must prove he is a partner for peace" by exerting his authority over his forces.

Israeli troops killed at least 39 Palestinians and Palestinian police shot to death at least 11 Israelis in running battles on Thursday, the bloodiest day in the West Bank and Gaza since Arafat set up his self-rule government.

Israel declared a state of emergency, deploying extra troops and sending in tanks and helicopters to quell the violence, the first time it had used tanks in the West Bank since it captured the territory in 1967, Israel Radio said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut short a European tour and asked for a meeting with Arafat to put an end to the violence, which appeared to have been triggered by Israel's opening of a tunnel adjacent to the al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock mosque complex, Islam's third holiest shrine, in disputed Arab East Jerusalem.
Israeli Finance minister Dan Meridor, also in New York, told investors at the New York Stock Exchange that he hoped Palestinians would act in a "sensible and responsible" way.
